subject.title: [Feature]: models.providers.*.enabled flag to disable providers without removing config

question: Should OpenClaw add a public `models.providers.<id>.enabled?: boolean` contract, and what should happen when the disabled provider is the selected primary or an explicit fallback?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds a public config option and changes provider routing/fallback semantics, which root policy treats as compatibility-sensitive product direction.

options.title: Approve shared provider eligibility
options.body: Add the config field and implement one shared eligibility helper across schema, planning, fallback, catalogs, auth/probe visibility, status output, docs, and tests, including disabled-primary semantics.

options.title: Reject provider-level disable
options.body: Keep the current model where operators remove provider blocks or edit model/fallback lists, avoiding another public config knob and its upgrade semantics.

options.title: Defer to provider lifecycle design
options.body: Hold this until provider enablement, plugin setup, auth/status, and model picker lifecycle behavior are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve shared provider eligibility
recommendation.body: Add the config field and implement one shared eligibility helper across schema, planning, fallback, catalogs, auth/probe visibility, status output, docs, and tests, including disabled-primary semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest history signal across model config, fallback, planning, and status surfaces where the shared contract would land.
